overviews.title: What is Textile Engineering?: Course Fees 2026, Subjects, Top Colleges, Admissions

blocks.value: Textile Engineering is an engineering specialization. It deals with designing, manufacturing, processing, and producing fabrics of different types. The focus of these courses is on the creation of unique and creative apparel, fabrics, yarns, fibers, cotton, fibers, yarns used in clothing articles. Textile Engineering courses are offered at various academic levels, including diploma, certificate, UG, PG, and doctorate . B.Tech and M.Tech. in textile engineering are some of the most sought-after courses in this field.

To be eligible for a textile engineering course, the most basic requirement is to pass class 12 PCM from a recognized board , with at least 50-60% aggregate score. Some of the most popular colleges offering a course in textile engineering include IIT Delhi, Anna University, ICT Mumbai, NIT Jalandhar, PSGCT Coimbatore and more. Besides the merit-based admission, some top colleges require entrance scores of exams like JEE Main, TNEA Counselling and GATE for admission to these courses at different levels.
After a course in textile Engineering, one can primarily work in areas of development and manufacture of textile fabric used in the apparel industry .

faqs.question: What is Textile Engineering?
faqs.answer: Textile Engineering is in growing demand due to diverse cultures and traditions around the world and it is one of the most popular disciplines in engineering/technology. "Textile Engineering" is a big research field of technology that deals with all activities of producing textile fabric & yarns which are involved in the process of textile manufacturing. It includes process engineering that spins around the garment, colour, and fabric line of industries. India is a large market for imports and exports of textile products, therefore the professionals trained in Textile Engineering are recruited by top companies.

faqs.question: Why should I study B.Tech Textile Engineering course?
faqs.answer: Reasons you can consider BTech Textile Engineering course: There are a lot of earning opportunities in this field as the customer demand for creative and innovative fashion products is continuously growing. You can create innovative and sustainable materials for clothing. In the automotive and aerospace industries , you'll develop lightweight textiles for interior and exterior parts. Also, in the medical field , you will be involved in creating advanced wound dressings and other stuff used for medical treatment purposes. You can also work for the betterment of the environment through textile recycling and reuse practices. Basically, you have so many opportunities after completing the BTech Textile Engineering course where you can learn, experiment, and innovate to meet the fashion expectations of customers. You will also be offered decent salary packages by the recruiters according to your skills and creative approach to work.

faqs.question: What are the core Textile Engineering subjects covered in the syllabus?
faqs.answer: The Textile Engineering subjects differ on the basis of the college offering the course and the course level at which you're planning to pursue the course. The Textile Engineering syllabus includes core subjects, electives, and project work. Some core Textile Engineering subjects are given below for your reference: Introduction to Textile Engineering and Technology Polymer Chemistry Fibre Science Yarn Manufacturing Technology of Textile Coloration Apparel Manufacturing Technology Theory of Textile Structures

faqs.question: How many B.Tech in Textile Engineering colleges are there in India?
faqs.answer: There are around 50 B Tech in Textile Engineering colleges in India . Out of these, 29 are private colleges and 20 are owned by the government . Popular govt. faqs.question: What is meant by Textile Engineering?

blocks.value: Textile manufacturing is a major industry across the globe. It is based on the conversion of fibre into yarn, yarn into fabric. Some of engineering colleges run specialized degree courses on Textile engineering.

The program in Textile Engineering primarily covers development and characterization of the polymeric raw materials and methods of conversion of the same into textile materials followed by further value addition and appropriate engineering processes into products.
Courses also include subjects related to the management of the textile production facilities. During first 3 semesters, the basics of engineering that is common to all branches is also taught.

faqs.question: What is the admission process to pursue various courses in Textile Engineering?

value: In this case, the admission process in Textile Engineering depends on the institute/college. Few of them might provide admission on merit while few follow the direct admission process.

Institutes providing admission to Textile Engineering BE/ BTech courses mostly follow the merit-based admission process. Textile Engineering is also a challenging field of engineering whcih requires skills such as creativity and excellent presence of mind in order to suggest changes to any issues pertaining to textile products. Candidates should also be quick-learners as well as ready to give in long hours of work in order to extract the right kind of fabric and produce bulk quantities as per the demand of the consignors.

faqs.question: Is there any entrance exam required for admission to BTech Textile Engineering?

blocks.value: Well, top colleges offering the BTech Textile Engineering course do need valid entrance exam scores with an excellent rank, but there are some colleges that also give admission on the basis of Class 12 board exam marks. Those colleges release merit cutoff lists and the shortlisted applicants are often called for an interview round, which serves as the final call for admission.
It is recommended to prepare for and give the entrance test to keep both options of admission to the course open with varied college choices to choose from.

faqs.question: Do I need to pay any application fee for admission to the BTech Textile Engineering course?

blocks.value: Yes , almost every college charges an application fee for admission to the BTech in Textile Engineering course that needs to be paid at the time of filling out the admission application form to complete the registration process. The average application fee ranges between INR 500 and INR 3,000 , which differs on the basis of the college offering the course and its overall ranking in India.
To know about the accurate fee structure, you can check the admission guidelines given on the respective college websites for students' reference.

faqs.question: Can I get lateral entry admission to the BTech Textile Engineering course?

blocks.value: Yes, you can easily get lateral entry admission to the BTech Textile Engineering and Technology course given that you have a 3-year engineering Diploma in a related discipline with at least 50% marks in the final exams and clear the lateral entry admission test . The lateral entry admissions are done on the basis of entrance exams conducted at the state or university level, which allows you to directly enter the 2 nd year of the B Tech Textile Engineering course .

A few colleges offering admission via lateral entry to the BTech Textile Engineering course are Uttar Pradesh Textile Technology Institute (UPTTI), Kanpur; Government College of Engineering and Textile Technology (Berhampore); and Nitra Technical Campus (Ghaziabad).

faqs.question: Do reserved category students get any marks relaxation for BTech Textile Engineering admission?

blocks.value: Almost every college offering the BTech Textile Engineering course gives some sort of relaxation in marks to students who belong to any of the reserved categories like the SC/ST/OBC/PwD. The relaxation in marks is generally 5%, which may vary based on the college reservation policies.
You can check the detailed admission guidelines and procedure on the respective college websites to avoid any confusion at the time of admission.

faqs.question: How much time is required to prepare for BTech Textile Engineering entrance exam?

blocks.value: There is no fixed time to prepare for BTech in Textile Engineering entrance. Try and start at least 8 to 10 months before the final entrance exam is tentatively scheduled to take place. This approach usually gives students an upper hand, as they can cover the maximum portion of the syllabus comfortably, practice previous year question papers, take mock tests, and go through a rigorous revision, increasing the chances of shortlisting.

faqs.question: Is BTech Textile Engineering syllabus the same across all top colleges?

blocks.value: No, the syllabus for the BTech Textile Engg. course is not the same across all top colleges in India . Every college follows a certain coursework pattern that is decided at the beginning of the academic session itself. The committee makes sure that the curriculum is updated as per the latest industry standards and covers both theoretical learning and practical knowledge. You can check the respective college websites for the official syllabus for the BTech Textile Engineering course.

blocks.value: Textile Engineering is one of the most popular engineering disciplines. Textile Engineering revolves around the garment, fabric, and colour industries. Textile Engineering comprises the principles, laws, and scientific processes applied in the production of textile fabrics and yarns of various types. It also comprises the study of scientific principles about the analysis of polymers involved in textile fibre synthesis. Numerous institutions and colleges have started textile manufacturing/Textile Engineering specialisation programs. Students in these courses learn about the interaction of material and machine, energy conservation, natural and synthetic materials, waste control, pollution and safety, and health. India offers the following four categories of Textile Engineering programs:

Studies, leading to an M.Tech with a period of two years following the completion of an undergraduate degree in engineering
Doctoral degree programs leading to a PhD with a duration of one to two years following the completion of the PG degree

blocks.value: List of Subjects in Textile Engineering

The following are some course details that will be taught to the students while they are taking the Textile Engineering Course. This is a detailed list of subjects that have been mentioned below. Have a look.

value: This chapter presents an overview of textile-related materials. You will explore the history and vocabulary of textiles while learning about the various types of textile fibres and fabrics through lectures taught by professionals. You will examine the various types of materials used in the production of textiles and related terminology and textile history. This chapter covers the types and properties of smart textiles, textile fibres, and the entire list below: Utilising nanotechnology in textile production. Understanding the many types of textile fabric. Comparing modern and ancient fabric textiles. The history of woven textiles and terminologies. Textile design for sustainability and fashion.

Testing textiles involves evaluating the quality and compatibility of raw materials and material selection. It is a crucial component of textile manufacturing, distribution, and consumption. Testing is the process of determining the qualities of various types of substances. An important aspect of the textile industry is testing. During textile testing, flaws in machinery and materials can be quickly identified. In addition, textile testing must ensure compliance with evolving government safety requirements and meet the rising demand for high-quality textiles and apparel among consumers. Proper testing can be conducted if a testing laboratory has the necessary equipment. Textile testing enables businesses, consumer groups, and the government to ensure that textiles are safe and of high quality, and the client receives value for their money. Textile items are manufactured globally and distributed to global markets. Testing ensures that dangerous or unlawful substances do not escape through regulatory gaps. This chapter will also cover the many types of textile testing equipment utilised within the textile industry.

We utilise items created using textile yarn every day. Textile yarn is a thread of fibres or filaments, either natural or manufactured. Fibre is a short strand of hair. Natural fibres such as wool from sheep, cotton and linen from plants, and silk from silkworms can be spun into textile yarn. It can also be fabricated from synthetic or man-made fibres, including nylon, acrylic, and polyester. In this chapter, you will gain an in-depth understanding of the yarn structure and the classifications of Textile Yarn.

In this chapter, students will learn about the preparation phase of textile materials, which is a crucial step in the manufacturing process. It is quite difficult to obtain the desired outcome in the dyeing, printing, and finishing processes without a preparation phase. After studying this chapter, students will be familiar with and able to comprehend industry terms, impurities contained in natural and synthetic fibres (Raw Cotton, Wool, Silk, Polyester, Nylon, and Acrylic), and their cost-effective removal. This subject also covers Chemical Treatment, Chemical Processes, and Process Flowcharts for Cotton, Wool, Silk, and Synthetic Fibres, as well as Basic Knowledge of Sizing, Desizing, Scouring, and Bleaching. Students will be able to know the steps involved in getting the ideal fabric quality once they have mastered this vocabulary.

The production of textiles is a significant industry. It relies heavily on transforming fibre into yarn and then yarn into fabric. In this chapter, you’ll learn how these are then coloured or printed and woven into cloth, ultimately transformed into apparel, home furnishings, upholstery, and other industrial products. Fabric choosing for a particular style or brand of clothing. The same style is frequently manufactured in multiple fabrics. In the textile and clothing sector, product quality is determined by the quality and standard of fibres, fabric construction, yarns, colour fastness, patterns, and finished products. Quality control in garment production, pre-sales and after-sales service, delivery, pricing, etc., is crucial for any garment manufacturer, trader, or exporter.
Computer Applications in the Textile Industries

The current era is the computerisation era. Every industry benefits from the automation and convenience of use provided by computer science. All of this has been grossly neglected by the textile industry, which is a major source of income for a country. The textile industry focuses primarily on designing and producing yarn, fabric, and apparel. The computer's application areas can be broadly categorised as engineering, business, scientific, and recreational. Computers are extensively employed in engineering applications to assist the designing and manufacturing industries in managing their processes and information systems. The computer's function in manufacturing can be broadly divided into two categories: design and process control. The introduction of the computer and its applications has transformed manufacturing practices in the textile sector. Product creation is more inventive than ever before. In addition, the amount of time required to generate a concept and then convert it into a final product has drastically decreased. There are several other benefits that manufacturing facilities enjoy. These are the topics covered in this section.

Filtration, bolting cloths for sifting and screening, press covers and nets for segregating lots during washing are all examples of processing fabrics used by various manufacturers. In this section, you’ll learn all about this in detail.

Materials and procedures used in the manufacturing of fabric dictate the features of the finished product, which is made of yarns and fibres. Weaving or knitting are the most common methods of interlacing used to make fabrics today. Printing, weaving, tracing embroidery, and colour-detailing are some of the techniques used in textile design to create the final product. Prototypes and virtual samples are developed after the procedure is conceptualised. Get to know more about those in this section.
Information Technology in the Textile Industry

The textile business relies heavily on information technology (IT). The four Ms (Men, Material, Machine, and Money) are employed in any manufacturing operation. Managers must work on synchronising and generating synergies with internal and external processes to achieve organisational success. As competition heats up, businesses are turning to information technology (IT) to help them improve their Supply Chain Management (SCM) and gain a strategic advantage. To put it simply, a growing number of textile companies are taking advantage of technology to improve their bottom line. Learn more about how IT plays a significant role in leveraging the Textile Industry.

Fabric is most commonly made by weaving or knitting. Non-woven fabrics such as felting, laminating, and bonding can also be used to create a product. Two strands are interlaced at right angles on a loom to weave a fabric. Weft yarns are the horizontal threads. Learn more about these methods of building and designing fabric in this section.

complete_article.text: Why do students choose to enroll in some engineering streams more? What affects the choice of engineering stream among the students? In this article, we have tried to understand which are some of themost popular engineering streamsamong the students and why.

Does the popularity of engineering streams depend on the job scenario? Experts believe that it is one of the major factors. With Information Technology (IT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) entering our everyday lives the demands for streams like computer science, Data Science, AI, etc have increased. However, the rise in popularity of oneengineering streamdoes not affect the importance of others. Till now,Computer Engineering is one of the most popular engineering streamsas per the All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE) report.

Over the past 5 years, enrollment in the computer engineering stream has increased from 9 lakhs to 11 lakhs. The core engineering branches are still the most popular choices among engineering candidates.Mechanical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Civil Engineering, and Electrical Engineering are the top 5 engineering streamswith the maximum number of enrollments at the undergraduate level over the past few years, as per AISHE.
Steadily, theengineering streams that are growing in popularity areInformation Technology,Chemical Engineering,Agriculture EngineeringandAeronautical Engineering.

Under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the combination of major and minor courses within the broader stream has been introduced. This helps the candidates select one specialisation and also pursue one minor specialisation alongside. With the demand of the job market, many top engineering colleges in India offer minor course combinations of AI, Data Science, Digital Engineering, and others.
